## bp

`bp` is a new stable skill in `skills/dev/bp`, included in the Claude Code plugin and the skills catalog. Type `/bp` and the agent opens, finds and remembers the apps, sites, files and folders you use every day, on macOS and Linux.

- Open an app, site, file or folder from a saved nickname: `/bp gmail`, `/bp chrome`, `/bp work`.
- Ask for a task that spans apps ("open Chrome, go to Gmail, send the report, then tell Wang in Slack"). The apps it had to open are saved automatically, so the next run needs one word.
- Find installed apps by name or by kind (`/bp find`, `/bp scan`, a drawing board, a browser, a terminal) and save the ones you pick.
- Group shortcuts to start or stop a whole work setup at once, and open the newest download or any file by name.
- Go straight to the right page with deep links for search, maps, mail drafts, calendar events and meetings, in the browser you name.
- Open a drawing board or editor and work in it live when the session has computer-control tools; without them it opens the app and says so, and never pretends to have drawn.
- Everything runs through one tested script that checks every value. A saved app must be an installed GUI app, links are limited to a safe list, and shortcut values are never run as shell commands. Auto-save keeps only plain site addresses, never a link to one email or one document.

## Install

Pick one installation route.

For Codex or a direct global skill installation:

```bash
npx skills@latest add itamaker/skills --skill=bp
```

Invoke `$bp` in Codex or `/bp` in Claude Code.

For the managed Claude Code plugin:

```text
/plugin marketplace add itamaker/skills
/plugin install itamaker-skills@itamaker
```

The plugin exposes `/itamaker-skills:bp`. Existing plugin users can update their marketplace and installed plugin to version 2.1.1.

## Requirements and limits

`bp` needs macOS or Linux with bash and installs nothing. Shortcuts live in `~/.bp/aliases.tsv`. Windows is not supported. Drawing or typing inside an app, and driving web pages, use the browser or computer-control tools of your session; the skill ships no automation of its own.
